summary: 62-year-old man on ibuprofen with 2 days of melaena and one coffee-ground vomit; HR 104, SBP 112, Hb 9.8 g/dL, urea 14 mmol/L. Glasgow-Blatchford 12: admit, resuscitate, endoscopy within 24 h.

inputs.hpi: Two days of black, tarry, offensive stools. Vomited once this morning — dark coffee-ground material. Mild epigastric discomfort for a week. Taking ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day for three weeks for low back pain. Light-headed on standing. No liver disease, no previous bleeding. Drinks about 10 units a week.

exam.general: Pale, alert. Pulse 104/min, BP 112/70 lying with a postural drop to 98 systolic. Capillary refill 3 s.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding. No stigmata of chronic liver disease. PR: black tarry stool (melaena).

inputs.socialHistory: Taxi driver. Smokes 10/day. Alcohol about 10 units/week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute upper GI bleed
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute upper GI bleed, haemodynamically stable after fluids, Glasgow-Blatchford 12 — probable NSAID-associated peptic ulcer, non-variceal.

emergencyLevel.note: GBS 12 is not low risk: admission and endoscopy within 24 h, same day.

redFlags.note: NSAID is the likely cause and must be stopped (clinician decision).
redFlags.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no red flag matched among 10 (ios.visitRisk, ios.allergyBanner, ios.triage, ios.radiation.redFlags, ios.radiation.urgencyNote, ios.pipeline.alert, ios.acuity)

mustInclude.note: Hb 9.8 with ongoing melaena: blood must be available.
Restrictive: transfuse at Hb ≤7 g/dL, target 7–9 g/dL (no cardiovascular disease).

ESGE suggests considering high-dose IV PPI before endoscopy; NICE CG141 advises against PPI before endoscopy. Post-endoscopy PPI for high-risk stigmata is agreed. Quality only because the sources disagree on the pre-endoscopy dose.

mustExclude.note: ESGE 2021 recommends against tranexamic acid in NVUGIH (HALT-IT: no mortality benefit, more venous thromboembolism).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove tranexamic acid from the upper_gi_bleed protocol medications (ESGE 2021 recommends against it; HALT-IT). Surgeon sign-off needed.

guideline.name: ESGE Guideline — endoscopic diagnosis and management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (NVUGIH), update 2021
guideline.section: GBS for pre-endoscopy risk stratification; restrictive transfusion (Hb ≤7 g/dL, target 7–9; ≤8 and target ≥10 with cardiovascular disease); early endoscopy ≤24 h after resuscitation; high-dose PPI; tranexamic acid not recommended; H. pylori testing
guideline.citation: Gralnek IM, Stanley AJ, Morris AJ, et al. Endoscopy. 2021;53:300–332.

guideline.name: NICE CG141 — Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
guideline.section: Blatchford at first assessment; endoscopy within 24 h of admission; no PPI before endoscopy for suspected non-variceal bleeding
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG141. London: NICE; 2012 (last updated 2016).

guideline.name: ACG Clinical Guideline — upper gastrointestinal and ulcer bleeding
guideline.section: Endoscopy within 24 h of presentation for hospitalised patients with UGIB
guideline.citation: Laine L, Barkun AN, Saltzman JR, Martel M, Leontiadis GI. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:899–917.

guideline.name: BSG-led multisociety consensus care bundle — early clinical management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Care bundle: risk assess with GBS; group and save / crossmatch; restrictive transfusion; OGD within 24 h
guideline.citation: Siau K, Hearnshaw S, Stanley AJ, et al. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2020;11:311–323.

guideline.name: Glasgow-Blatchford score — derivation
guideline.section: Score components: urea, Hb (sex-specific), SBP, HR, melaena, syncope, hepatic disease, cardiac failure
guideline.citation: Blatchford O, Murray WR, Blatchford M. A risk score to predict need for treatment for upper-gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Lancet. 2000;356:1318–1321.

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid did not reduce death from GI bleeding and increased venous thromboembolic events
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

guideline.name: NICE CG184 — Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and dyspepsia in adults: investigation and management
guideline.section: Stop NSAIDs in peptic ulcer disease where possible
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG184. London: NICE; 2014 (last updated 2019).

guideline.name: Maastricht VI/Florence consensus report — management of Helicobacter pylori infection
guideline.section: Test for H. pylori in peptic ulcer bleeding; re-test if negative in the acute setting
guideline.citation: Malfertheiner P, Megraud F, Rokkas T, et al. Gut. 2022;71:1724–1762.

rationale: Index non-variceal bleed with a clearly high Glasgow-Blatchford score (urea 14 → 4, Hb 9.8 male → 6, HR ≥100 → 1, melaena → 1; total 12). A concordant consultation recognises the bleed, escalates to same-day/admission, recommends the GBS, prepares blood, and plans endoscopy within 24 h with PPI and a restrictive transfusion strategy, without tranexamic acid.
